source: Joshi and Parpola 1987, CISI1, official IGNCA scan https://ignca.gov.in/Asi_data/76884.pdf
method: Manual source photographs inspected in catalogue order. The Mayig unknown marker determined the candidate frame, but no Lipi alternative readings or root/methods restoration predictions were consulted before this record. Original seals and their mirrored impressions are both inspected when present. No image alteration.
critical_schema_fact: P000 represents a section of significant damage or lost material, with a percent_lost feature. One P000 element does not imply one lost sign.

observations.reason: Large missing/eroded upper-left portion in the normalized impression. Only a decorated diamond and nearby short strokes survive clearly; lost glyph count is unbounded.
Unknown portion is at the broken right end of the normalized text. Partial curved carving survives, but the missing corner does not independently exclude additional lost units.

Partly visible terminal graphic at the left border of the normalized impression. Several diagonal/vertical strokes survive, but the edge-truncated form does not independently constrain the entire lost span to exactly one glyph.
Broken left end of normalized impression; a partial curved unit may survive, but additional lost content cannot be excluded.
Text loss is at the broken left edge of the normalized impression; surviving diagonal strokes do not establish a one-unit lost span.
Damaged rightmost corner of normalized impression, beyond a short-stroke cluster. Edge loss does not establish exactly one glyph.
Normalized left end is broken, with a small vertical/curved remnant; the missing end has unknown lost extent.
A tall vertical remnant remains to the right of a complex graphic unit, but the top-right corner is lost and the total terminal span is not constrained independently.
Large triangular loss at the right end of the normalized text, beyond the surviving leaf-like unit. One P000 compresses an unknown lost span.
A broad surface spall removes much of the right portion of the normalized text. A short-stroke remnant remains at the far right; multiple intervening units could be lost.
Large triangular missing portion at the left end of the normalized impression; text span is not one glyph.
Broad upper/right loss in the original seal photograph; a large lost text span cannot be constrained to one unit.
Damaged left terminal region in the normalized impression. Partial carving survives but is close to an irregular edge; the full lost span is not independently bounded.

Internal spall between a jar-like graphic and decorated diamond-like graphic. Its width and residual diagonal traces do not exclude two narrow units or a compound; the one-slot assumption would rely on transcription conventions.

An internal partially eroded group is spatially bounded by a short-stroke cluster on its left and two full-height vertical strokes on its right in the normalized impression. The surrounding top text surface and both delimiters survive. The visible remnants occupy approximately one neighboring full-height graphic span.
observations.visible_constraints: At least two descending near-vertical/slanted carved segments with small upper/middle projections survive inside the bounded interval. The lower portions are distinguishable from the animal horn below. No large blank hole or broken exterior edge lies inside this interval.
observations.uncertainty: One graphic unit is a cautious segmentation judgment, not proof that it represented one linguistic sign. A compact compound or special variant remains possible; exact identity is not assigned.

observations.reason: Small surviving corner with decorated diamond and short-stroke remnants; most of the seal and terminal text extent are lost.
Normalized left end survives only as a partial curved remnant at a broken edge. Additional lost end content cannot be excluded.

scope_limit: This is a small purposeful source audit, not a random accuracy assessment. Failure to obtain eight candidates is preferable to assuming unknown damage markers each encode one sign. No proposed restored code or meaning is supplied by this file.
